sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.markdown:
FY2024A/FY2025A are audited LK lines (dossier); FY2026-28E are the coverage model's forecasts (fund record), from 300 kt flat volume [S3/F1], realisation 0.758 of the new-series deck [S8/S15], cash cost Rp7.99m/t +2.5% IDR [S7], 30% payout [S12]. Revenue Rp5,989/6,665/6,646bn; EBIT Rp2,295/2,854/2,748bn; net income Rp2,189/2,712/2,700bn; EPS Rp321/398/396; DPS Rp96/119/119. Net cash Rp8,516bn, zero bank debt [F37]. 10y FCFF DCF (COE 11.18%, g 2.5%) discounts the deck then USD 1,150/t real; the bridge adds cash/associates, deducts trapped cash, buyback and related-party charges. Base Rp4,883/sh, bear Rp2,116, bull Rp9,385.

Answers: (1) The related-party deployment charge at 1.0, not 0.25, costs another Rp110/sh, NAV ~Rp4,773 — survives. (2) The Rp750bn buyback comes from operating cash flow: FY2026E FCF ~Rp1,840bn covers the ~Rp657bn dividend plus Rp750bn at ~1.3x. (3) At the CPO band floor the estate is worth Rp2,116/sh and the payout survives only at ~Rp31-42/sh, down ~65% — the carry leg fails, so the kill leg pays no dividend.

**Entry and payoff.** Rp1,590 is the limit — one tick under the 13-Nov close of Rp1,595, not a wait trigger (3% max chase to Rp1,638). The 3-year EV is 71.9% (p_up 0.42 at the archetype prior; up +207.1% to the unchanged Rp4,883; down -32.4% to the Rp1,075 kill; 3.72% pa dividend on the up leg; 1.0% drag). The kill is a falsification level, not a stop: the break is the Rp1,434/sh cash-plus-associates backing (Rp8,516bn net cash + Rp1,261bn associates = Rp9,777bn / 6,819.96m), ARB-filled one 25% band lower at Rp1,075 (the fund rules). up/|down| 6.4 vs the library's 2.14 — the width is the tape, not the model: target and p_up are unchanged, the gap carried in size. own-Kelly 1.02 full / 0.25 quarter; library-Kelly 0.43.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.markdown: The market treats LSIP as the Salim group's thinly-traded planter whose earnings are CPO beta and whose Rp8.5tn cash is discounted because the group controls its deployment — a persistent holdco-style discount.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** At Rp1,595 the market pays Rp10.88tn for Rp8.52tn net cash and Rp1.26tn of associates, valuing the operating estate at ~Rp1.10tn — 0.46x FY2025 EBITDA, 0.41x FY2026E, or Rp161/sh. It implies CPO ~USD640/t, 52% of the deck's FY2027E USD1,240/t [reverse DCF], and 5.0x FY2026E / 4.0x FY2027E EPS; the FY2026E dividend yield is 6.0%, 7.5% on FY2027E, against an 11.18% COE. That prices a permanent sub-cycle CPO path or cash that never reaches minorities.

**Why wrong:** Cash is 78% of market cap, debt is zero, FY2025 FCF covered the dividend 5.8x, and the through-cycle DCF is Rp4,883/sh after charging the related-party risks — 3.1x the tape. The 6%+ yield is the market's own anchor; it exceeds the COE only if the payout is not trusted. That is a governance discount, not an estate worth Rp161/sh, and coverage lag below the top-40 keeps it there.

**Why the tape is 25% below the bear case.** Rp1,595 is 24.6% under the Rp2,116 bear DCF, so the discount is a claim on the cash, not on CPO. Three things would prove the market right: the related-party deployment charge landing at 1.0 — though even that costs another Rp110/sh (NAV Rp4,773), a fraction of a Rp521/sh gap; the Rp750bn buyback funded from trapped rather than operating cash (FY2026E FCF Rp1,840bn covers dividend and buyback at 1.3x, i.e. operating); and the CPO deck floor not holding, a sustained sub-USD900/t print cutting the payout to Rp31–42/sh. Thin liquidity lets the discount persist. I cannot close the residual with a DCF — it is a trust discount, and belongs in p_up 0.42 and size, not a shaded target.

**What proves us wrong:** CPO sustained below ~USD900/t (Kemendag reference), related-party deployment above Rp1,000bn on non-market terms, DPS below Rp80, or volume below 255kt.

sections.heading: House coverage reconciliation
sections.markdown: FY2026-28E estimates match coverage/companies/LSIP.JK/model.json exactly: revenue Rp5,989/6,665/6,646bn, EBIT Rp2,295/2,854/2,748bn, EPS Rp321/398/396, DPS Rp96/119/119. The levels differ because the methods do. My Rp4,883 is a DCF-only base at USD1,150/t real, 3% below the house DCF Rp5,044; the house Rp4,689 is a 50/25/25 scenario blend of 60/25/15 DCF/EV-EBITDA/P/BV, and the 6.2x peer EV/EBITDA (Rp3,616) and P/BV (~Rp2,366) legs drag it below the DCF. I drop them: 6.2x capitalises trailing operating EV and P/BV is historical cost, not replacement. the three-item bridge is identical (trapped cash Rp196bn, buyback Rp351bn, deployment Rp250bn); the section-4 FX caveat does not touch a direct DCF.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.markdown:
1. Related-party gravity: 63.26% of revenue sold to parent SIMP [S7/F34]; Rp665.016bn of cash at Bank Ina Perdana [F53]. Optics-class, disclosed; but the core reason the cash may never reach minorities.
2. Parent-driven working capital: operating NWC went 7.3% of revenue (FY2023) → 21.7% (FY2024) → 3.3% (FY2025) [S0/F34]; the bear assumes 2x the FY2025 ratio.
3. Cost and volume risk: FY2025 cash cost rose 21% to Rp7.791m/t as external FFB purchases reached Rp672.3bn [S7]; GAPKI warns El Nino could cost 3m tonnes nationally, heaviest in 2027 [S24/F68]. Base volume is flat at 300 kt.
4. No growth asset base: 110,982 ha in 2025 vs 114,111 in 2021, 7% immature [F32] — a capital-return story.
5. Peak-margin risk: FY2025's 35.4% EBIT margin is near the four-year high [dossier]; the archetype's dominant failure is buying at peak margin; the through-cycle DCF is the defence.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: Early 2030: the position lost ~32%. Most likely: the El Nino premium unwinds, CPO falls to ~USD 887/t and stays there as stocks rebuild; the 2027 FFB shortfall cuts volume 15% while cash cost stays at the FY2025 step-up; the group deploys part of the Rp8.5tn pile into a related-party asset at a value-destroying price, so the trapped-cash discount never closes. The payout is maintained on ~Rp31-42/sh and the market keeps a governance discount on 63% parent revenue. An ARB-locked kill fills one to two bands below the Rp1,434 break, past -32.4%.

sections.markdown:

But 30-Sep-26 net cash Rp8,516bn has no dossier line (FY2025 cash Rp7,597.5bn, L32); cited [F37/S8], plausible on 9M NI Rp1,744.9bn, but unverified — the floor rests on it. [MATERIAL]

3. **Variant perception.** Rp4,883 is the house DCF (Rp5,044), 4.1% over TP Rp4,689 — bottom-up restates house view; the priors line already states the bear case. At 1,590, 6.1% yield +2.5% g = 8.6% < 11.18% COE: all return is the re-rating. catalyst_date null; the only dated event is the buyback expiring 31-Dec-2026. [MATERIAL]

4. **Base rate/sleeve.** No capex cycle: flat 300kt, hectares 114,111→110,982 since 2021, 35.4% EBIT margin at a 4y high — the archetype's stated dominant failure. Honest key: holdco_discount_narrowing (0.33, n=25). Sleeve COVERAGE; per-sleeve calibration known-missing — no hit rate claimed. [MATERIAL]

5. **Sizing/ARB.** 1,075 < 1,590 < 4,883 coheres, but -32.4% is not ARB-sized: it concedes a second locked session fills Rp806 (-49.3%), where quarter-Kelly is ~0.14% NAV. The falsification level (bear DCF 2,116) is +33% above entry, so the down state is a governance tail; p_down 0.58 carries the trade. [MATERIAL]

6. **New fact.** From 1-Jan-2027 all palm-oil exports route via the DSI platform with a per-service USD fee (Kemendag, 12-Nov-2026) — unmodelled 2027+ cost. [MATERIAL]

7. **Pre-mortem steelman.** Avoided mode: the group swaps cash into a related-party asset at a premium — a permanent NAV cut, not a price break. Every exit is price-triggered, so a deal holding the tape above Rp1,075 never fires; deployment is "review", not exit. [MATERIAL]

8. **Anti-gaming.** stage_log clean (draft stamp matches estimates_committed_at); sizing null leaves "gap carried in size" unverified; Rp1,595 is called the "13-Nov close" at 13:21 WIB, pre-close — an intraday mark; QC note. [MINOR]

**Stop objecting at** ≤Rp1,434/sh (par cash+associates), or Rp1,590 only with p_up 0.33, down -49.3%, deployment at 1.0, size ≤0.25% NAV.

**Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION.** "At Rp1,590 the carry is 8.6% against an 11.18% COE: the 207% up-leg is a 3.1x re-rating with no catalyst, and the only modelled loss is a governance event the price kill cannot see."

**Stop objecting at** ≤Rp1,434, trigger re-based below entry (0.10 multiplier/0.25% encoded); at 1,590 the payoff is COE and the kill is a stress fill.

**Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION.** "At 1,590 the revision clears its own cost of equity by twelve basis points — a 207% up-leg priced at the probability of a modest discount narrowing, a 49% loss charged at two-thirds weight, and a 0.25% position that cannot pay for the research."
